title: Phrasal verbs 2: in/out
subtitle: get in / get out, drop in, fill in, eat out
summary: Use phrasal verbs with in and out for movement into and out of places, and learn common verbs such as drop in, join in, eat out and get out of.

left.label: in = into a room, a building, a car etc.
left.text: In the same way you can say go in, come in, walk in, break in etc.
examples: Here's a key, so you can **let yourself in**.
Lisa walked up to the edge of the pool and **dived in**. (= into the water)
I've got a new apartment. I'm **moving in** on Friday.
As soon as I got to the airport, I **checked in**.

right.label: out = out of a room, a building, a car etc.
right.text: In the same way you can say go out, get out, move out, let somebody out etc.
examples: Stay in the car. Don't **get out**.
I had no key, so I was **locked out**.
She swam up and down the pool, and then **climbed out**.
Andy opened the window and **looked out**.
We paid the hotel bill and **checked out**.

lesson.heading: in / into and out / out of
lesson.text: Use **in** and **out** on their own. When you name the place, use **into** and **out of**.

examples.text: I'm **moving into** my new flat on Friday.

lesson.heading: Other verbs + in
lesson.text: **drop in** = visit somebody at home without arranging it. **join in** = take part in something that is already going on. **plug in** an electrical machine = connect it to the electricity supply.

examples.text: I **dropped in** to see Chris on my way home.
They were playing cards, so I **joined in**.
The fridge isn't working because you haven't **plugged it in**.

lesson.heading: take somebody in, fill in / fill out
lesson.text: **take somebody in** = deceive somebody. **fill in** or **fill out** a form, a questionnaire etc. = write the necessary information on it. Both fill in and fill out are correct.

examples.text: The man said he was a policeman and I believed him. I was completely **taken in**.
Please **fill in** the application form and send it to us by 28 February. or Please **fill out** the application form ...

lesson.heading: Other verbs + out
lesson.text: **eat out** = eat at a restaurant, not at home. **drop out of** college / a course / a race = stop before you have completely finished. **get out of** something that you arranged to do = avoid doing it.

examples.text: There wasn't anything to eat at home, so we decided to **eat out**.
Gary went to university but **dropped out** after a year.
I promised I'd go to the wedding. I don't want to go, but I can't **get out of** it now.

lesson.heading: leave out, cross out
lesson.text: **leave something out** = omit it, not include it. **cross something out** = write a line through it.

examples.text: In the sentence 'She said that she was ill', you can **leave out** the word 'that'.
Some of the names on the list had been **crossed out**.

lesson.text: Remember the pronoun rule: **plug it in**, **fill them in**, **cross it out**, **let us in** - the pronoun goes between the verb and in/out.

exercises.prompt: Lisa doesn't like cooking, so she ___ a lot.
exercises.explanation: eat out = eat at a restaurant, not at home.

exercises.prompt: If you're in our part of town, you should ___ and say hello.
exercises.explanation: drop in = visit somebody at home without arranging it.

exercises.prompt: Could you ___ this questionnaire? It will only take five minutes.
exercises.explanation: fill in or fill out a form / a questionnaire - both are possible.

exercises.prompt: Which word is missing: in, into or out?

items.text: We arrived at the hotel and checked ___.
When are you moving ___ your new flat?
The car stopped and the driver got ___.
Thieves broke ___ the house and stole some jewellery.
How did the thieves break ___? Through a window?
He opened his wallet and something fell ___.
I've got a new flat. I'm moving ___ on Friday.
Stay in the car. Don't get ___.

exercises.prompt: Kate was angry and walked ___ the meeting.
exercises.explanation: When you name the place (the meeting), use out of: walked out of the meeting.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrasal verb with its meaning.

pairs.right: take part in something already going on
stop a course or race before the end

exercises.prompt: Not all the runners finished the race. Three of them ___.
exercises.explanation: drop out (of a race / a course) = stop before you have finished.

exercises.prompt: Some people in the crowd started singing. Then a few more people ___ and soon everybody was singing.
exercises.explanation: join in = take part in something that is already going on.

exercises.statement: The man said he was a policeman and I believed him. I was completely taken in.
exercises.explanation: Correct. be taken in = be deceived.

exercises.prompt: 'I've made a mistake on this form.' Tell your friend what to do.
exercises.answer: Just cross it out and correct it.
exercises.explanation: cross it out - the pronoun goes between cross and out.

exercises.prompt: I can't avoid going to the party. In other words, I can't ___ going to the party.
exercises.explanation: get out of something = avoid doing something you arranged to do.

exercises.statement: The fridge isn't working because you haven't plugged in it.
exercises.explanation: ... because you haven't plugged it in. A pronoun object goes between the two parts of the phrasal verb.
